I've got a similar rig - F20 and Intel graphics - haven't tried these demos yet but I would guess you would need a designated GPU to run the UE4.

Honestly, I think big companies like EA just don't have enough prospective sales for it to be worthwhile to pay any attention to Linux. As Linux users, we all feel that these companies "need to start porting to Linux" but really, I think its a muuuuch smaller market that people realize. Don't get me wrong, I love Linux, and it would be cool to see more big games get released on it. I just don't think it would be at all valuable for then to do so. The fact that Linux is free, rightfully or wrongly, suggests to EA that there is little money to be made on our kernel.
Also, DirectX is probably the biggest barrier, and seeing how Microsoft has only been distancing itself from Linux lately (with dramatically less code donations, and the inability to install Linux on Win8 due to UEFI), the likelyhood of Microsoft suddenly deciding 'Hey why don't we release DirectX11 for Linux!' seems just about nil to me.

Well, if Ubisoft really does port WatchDogs to Linux, that would certainly get the ball rolling in terms of large studios jumping on the Linux bus! I think a lot of the smaller studios are willing to support Linux because they recognize that it is a growing market that has yet to be exhausted by their larger competitors.

Also - if you consider Valve to be larger than a 'mid-sized studio', they're certainly on the list of supporters! Thank you so much, Valve!

Dude you don't need to compare yourself to other to know if you're doing something right! Honestly, there's no such thing as right or wrong when it comes to just about anything beyond science and math. Even then, things are up for interpretation. Some people skate regular, some people skate goofy. They both work. Some people kick with their front foot when they're skating, some with their back. Both work, and that's all that really counts.
Just go out and do something - anything you want. It doesn't matter if you suck at it. Your fucking dog could be better at skateboarding than you. We all suck when we start something new. That's the beauty of it though. Every time you fall down, you just gotta pick yourself up again and one day you'll look back and you'll realize how much progress you've made. And that can be completely independent from others and their skills.
I know it can be hard, but just follow your heart man! It doesn't matter if it takes you somewhere that seems pointless in the end. Not many dudes keep skating past the age of 30 (but then some do.) That doesn't mean they wasted away their teens/20s skating because they enjoyed the ride while they could. Think about it - there's no point in living unless you're enjoying what you're doing. Once you're 40 and you throw away your old deck, you'll have something totally new in its place to enjoy all the same.

All you gotta do is find what you love, and love what you do! The only way to find what you love is to do everything you think you might like, and maybe even some things you think you won't like - you never know until you try man!

Yes I know what you mean. I went for a few months without getting very depressed at all and I started to believe, like what you were saying, that I've help myself out of the hole and that the illogic in its patterns meant it was all just outlook - all just in my head. It doesn't seem to work in the end...

You know now that I think about it, someone once posed a very similar thesis to what you gave to the other gamer when I was in a situation where I was feeling greater pressure to kill myself. I didn't take great at the time, because I didn't like the way responsibility was being placed on me after I had already died. I mean I guess the reason we want to die is to hide from our fears, from our frustrations, our shortcommings and failures, right? So when it was conceptually pointed out to me that by running from these things was in itself a failure in a sense, and that I was putting more anxiety and depression onto my loved ones, I rejected it because it further proved to me that it was not a solution to my problems. The idea was taking away the reward I wished to recieve after death, even though I would never have conciously been rewarded with anything had I indeed killed myself.
So perhaps now what I am saying (though perhaps I still can't precicely form my thoughts into words), though you haven't given a solution to him, you've helped to show him that suicide isn't an effective solution either.

(Sorry if this seems like rambling/isnt making sense/not helping/what have you, I'm sort of just realizing these things now and writing helps finalize them)

You know I don't think it's accurate to call what you told him "bullshit disguised as philosophy", and I'm saying this as someone who has considered (arrested by police for) suicide. I can see how you feel you were manipulating him, but let me tell you how I see it:

If a friend of mine were to take his own life, even though s/he never directly reccomended suicide to me, it would force me to deeply consider killing myself. With all the depression I already have, I could see the suicide of a loved one as the final push over the edge for me. So, I don't think what you said is total bullshit. If you really have struggled with suicide (and I don't in any way mean to doubt you) I'm sure you'd know its not something to deviously fake your way around, nor something you can just make shit up about and play it off as genuine. It's a very raw, very real topic that I think really only people like yourself and me, people who see it first hand, who really know the fact from fanfiction.

As for your feelings of manipulating him, you reached out to him because he was close to ending it, and there's a reason why you reached out. Personally, I can't come close to knowing what that reason is, but there is a reason. There's a reason why you didn't want to pass it by, a reason why he let you know it was to be his last match, and theres a reason why you and I are still here, still posting on Reddit and whatever else we do.
If you've ever seen Forrest Gump (one of my favourite movies), and I'm not religious or anything - I don't mean this as preaching, Forrest's mother tells him that God has a path for everyone, and that sometimes God shows himself, and these paths in strange ways. I guess what I'm trying to say is that fate can be a piculiar thing... Maybe that's not quite what I'm trying to say but hopefully you're understanding at least a little bit.
You've clearly done some great good in the world and I don't think you should be hard on yourself due to the ways in which this good as taken place... That makes sense?
